# Karnataka to Launch Innovation Museum, AI University, Boost Startups

By By Rediff Money Desk, Bengaluru

Jul 24, 2026 16:56

Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge announces MIST, AI University, and increased funding for deep-tech startups. The state aims to lead in AI and innovation.

Bengaluru, July 24 (PTI) Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge on Friday announced a slew of initiatives, including the launch of MIST (Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology), the Innovers Foundation, enhanced funding for deep-tech startups under Elevate Next, a proposed AI University, and the Nipuna Karnataka skilling programme, ahead of the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS).  
  
The summit will be held from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC) under the theme 'AI & Beyond', the Minister who holds the Information Technology, Biotechnology and Home portfolios, said.  
  
The minister also announced the constitution of a Deep Tech Working Group, a Government First policy to make government datasets available to startups through a regulatory sandbox, and said Karnataka would continue to position itself as the country's leading destination for artificial intelligence and deep-tech innovation.  
  
"AI may be the current buzzword, but Karnataka has always led emerging technologies and will continue to lead the next phase of artificial intelligence. BTS will serve as a platform for policy discussions, strategic decisions and the preparation of a blueprint not only for Karnataka but also for the country," Kharge told reporters.  
  
Kharge said the government has launched the Innovers Foundation to mentor revenue-generating deep-tech startups, help them access global markets and facilitate the adoption of their innovations by the government through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model.  
  
Reiterating that the next decade would be Karnataka's "Deep Tech Decade", he said the government has doubled funding for deep-tech startups under Elevate Next, increasing the maximum grant from Rs 50 lakh to Rs one crore.  
  
He said 983 applications were received, from which 33 deep-tech startups were selected and awarded grants totalling Rs 33 crore. Of these, 24 startups are from Bengaluru, one each from Hoskote, Udupi, Bidar and Hubballi, while five are from Delhi, Maharashtra and Telangana.  
  
"What is particularly encouraging is that 12 of the 33 startups are women-led," Kharge said, adding that grants ranged from Rs 85 lakh to Rs one crore.  
  
The minister also announced the formation of a Deep Tech Working Group/Vision Group, led by industry representatives, to strengthen Karnataka's deep-tech ecosystem.  
  
Announcing MIST, Kharge said part of the old NGF factory premises in Bengaluru would be transformed into India's first Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology at an estimated cost of Rs 300 crore under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model.  
  
He said the project would preserve the heritage factory structure and would be designed by Dublin-based architectural firm Heneghan Peng, known for designing the Grand Egyptian Museum.  
  
Kharge said the proposed Government First policy would allow startups and companies to access government datasets and public digital infrastructure through a regulatory sandbox, with the government becoming the first customer for viable solutions developed using public data.  
  
He also announced plans to establish a state-of-the-art AI University, developed in partnership with industry, think tanks and private companies, to focus on skilling, upskilling, research and development, incubation and global collaborations.  
  
Drawing a parallel with the Indian Institute of Science, Kharge said the proposed AI University would create a globally competitive ecosystem for artificial intelligence, adding that a detailed blueprint would be ready within 15 to 20 days.  
  
Addressing concerns over AI-led job disruptions, the minister said the government was rolling out Nipuna Karnataka, which he described as India's largest reskilling and upskilling programme, with an outlay of over Rs 300 crore.  
  
He said the industry-led programme aims to ensure 70 per cent placement and 100 per cent employability, equipping professionals with skills needed in emerging technologies as automation and artificial intelligence reshape the workforce.  
  
Kharge also said Karnataka was finalising a framework for the responsible use of artificial intelligence in governance and was preparing a Sustainable Data Centre Policy to promote environmentally sustainable technologies such as liquid cooling while ensuring future data centres have access to renewable energy and adequate water resources.

Source: PTI

title: Karnataka’s upcoming IT policy, expected to be finalised by July, marks a strategic pivot toward emerging technologies, with a ₹50 crore investment proposal for an Applied AI Centre over the next… | AIM
content:
Karnataka’s upcoming IT policy, expected to be finalised by July, marks a strategic pivot toward emerging technologies, with a ₹50 crore investment proposal for an Applied AI Centre over the next five years. State IT Minister Priyank M Kharge told The Economic Times that the new policy will move beyond Bengaluru, focusing on decentralising growth and building digital infrastructure in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. “The IT policy will focus on creating new economic accelerators beyond Bengaluru. Infrastructure is a problem with any growing city, and that was quite naturally raised by stakeholders,” Kharge noted. Cities like Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, and Kalaburagi are poised to benefit from this expansion. The policy includes a ₹300 crore fund-of-funds for startups and a ₹100 crore deep-tech fund. Supported by inputs from Ekroop Caur, the state IT secretary, and Nasscom, the draft envisions fostering innovation ecosystems across the state. Nasscom has also proposed a deep-tech fund structure with ticket sizes ranging from ₹50-₹200 crore to meet global standards. As the state gears up for the annual CEO meet, the draft policy is undergoing final reviews through the IT Vision Group. With a focus on AI, blockchain, IoT, and 5G, Karnataka is redefining its digital future with a forward-looking and inclusive IT strategy.

# Deep tech gets a shot in the arm, new IT policy and AI centre on the cards

## The government also intends to set aside ₹300 crore for a Fund-of-Funds

Updated  - March 11, 2025 10:51 am IST - Bengaluru

Shilpa Elizabeth

Subscribe to The Hindu @ Just ₹1\*

\*Offer only for new subscribers

The government intends to develop start-up ecosystems in Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad and Kalaburagi.
| Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto

The Karnataka government has announced that it will earmark a corpus fund of ₹100 crore for deep tech development in the State.

Advertisement

Advertisement

It also intends to set aside ₹300 crore for a Fund-of-Funds, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah announced in the Budget on Friday. The announcement comes against the backdrop of demands for sector-specific and region-specific Fund-of-Funds ever since the launch of the scheme by the Union government in 2016 with a corpus of ₹10,000 crore.

Both initiatives will be introduced under the Local Economy Accelerator Programme, which the government plans to launch to stimulate innovation and entrepreneurship in cities other than Bengaluru in the current year with a grant of ₹1,000 crore. LEAP will aim at creating 5 lakh employment opportunities.

#### Beyond Bengaluru

Under the programme, the government also intends to develop start-up ecosystems in Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad and Kalaburagi and set up incubators, accelerators, centres of excellence and Global Technology Centres.

Sign up for free and get curated news updates

SUBSCRIBE NOW

In recent years, the government has been increasingly pushing to develop start-up clusters and build investor interest in cities other than Bengaluru through its ‘Beyond Bengaluru’ initiatives. In 2024, Minister for Information Technology Priyank Kharge revealed the government’s intention to create 10,000 new start-ups in smaller towns and cities in five years under the initiative.

#### AI centre

During the Budget, the CM also announced that a new IT policy would be implemented in 2025 with the aim of further strengthening the State’s presence in the It sector.

“This new policy will not only give emphasis on cloud computing and development of emerging technologies but also expand information technology to tier-2 and tier-3 cities while reinforcing Karnataka’s position as a global technology hub,” he said.

To make further strides in the field of Artificial Intelligence, the government is also planning to set up a Centre for Applied AI for Tech Solutions with an investment of Rs 50 crores over the next five years.

The other major announcements include Global Innovation Districts in Mysuru, Belagavi, Dharwad and Bengaluru, three new GTCs in Mangaluru, Hubli and Belagavi, and an Agri-Tech accelerator in Kalaburagi.
